logline: The first female student council president of a formerly all-boys high school secretly moonlights at a maid cafe to keep her family afloat - until the school's most popular boy discovers her secret.

renewal.note: The 26-episode anime adaptation aired April-September 2010. The source manga by Hiro Fujiwara concluded in 2013. No second season has been produced.

bollymeter.basis: IMDb rates the series 7.9; reviewers consistently cite its snappy comedic delivery and strong romantic chemistry between the leads as the series' genuine strength, while acknowledging its shallow emotional depth and rushed finale.

seasons.review_body: Kaichou wa Maid-sama! aired on TBS from April 2010 as J.C.Staff's adaptation of Hiro Fujiwara's manga, and became one of the defining shojo romance anime of its era. The premise - a hard-edged female student council president with a secret maid cafe job, caught by the school's effortlessly popular boy - is a textbook tsundere setup, and the series knows it. What distinguishes it from formula is the comedic delivery: the show's sharp, snappy writing keeps the gags landing even in retrospect. Misaki Ayuzawa is a more competent and less passive female lead than many contemporaries, which gives the romance a different flavour - she drives as many scenes as she is rescued from. IMDb's 7.9 audience score reflects genuine warmth toward the series. The consistent critical point is a rushed ending and limited emotional depth; resolutions arrive in one or two episodes and the 26-episode run ends before the manga's full arc. The OVA adds some closure, but the anime adaptation is incomplete relative to its source. As a comfort rewatch - clever, fast, and charming - it holds.

episode_reviews.title: I am the Student Council President!
episode_reviews.spoiler_free: The series opener efficiently establishes Misaki's dual life and brings Usui into her orbit with the minimum of setup. The comedic timing is established immediately - J.C.Staff's direction keeps the pacing crisp throughout.
episode_reviews.the_moment: Usui's discovery of Misaki at the cafe - the central secret exposed in the first episode, letting the real dynamic begin.

episode_reviews.title: The Special Maid-sama!
episode_reviews.spoiler_free: The anime finale delivers emotional resolution but feels compressed relative to the manga's full arc. The ending is fast and the pacing is rushed - but it closes the central romantic question with enough warmth to satisfy.
episode_reviews.the_moment: The final rooftop scene - the culmination of the Misaki/Usui dynamic the series spent 26 episodes building.
